Definition: Achitub, the name of several priests
BiblicalUsage: Ahitub is named as a priestly father: Ahiah his son wore the ephod with Saul's army, and Ahimelech his son was the priest of Nob whom Saul murdered, and through him runs the line that leads to Zadok.
TheologicalSignificance: There is no teaching in this name alone. But the line it anchors matters: from Eli's house to Zadok's, the priesthood passed through fathers and sons, and God kept the line even when kings cut it down.
RelatedPeople: Ahimelech; Ahitub, Father of Zadok; Eli
